clue.text: Rumours going round regularly fall for dieters' concerns

indicators.note: the word for rumours encircles the picked letters, so it is wrapped around them

parts.note: a cry can mean a report or rumour going about, as in 'the cry is that...'

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the words fall for, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Gossip doing the rounds about slimmers falling for some fad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' looks like a verb with 'for'; together they are just the letter source for 'regularly'. A cry can mean a rumour, as in 'the hue and cry'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slimmers count the energy units in their food, so these are what people on a diet worry about.

clue.text: Rough path reportedly

indicators.note: as people say, so the answer sounds like the word for path

parts.note: a course is a route or path

explanation.surface: A bumpy track, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse means rough in texture, not smooth or fine.

clue.text: Measures left tiers altered

indicators.note: changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Steps taken after rows of seating were rearranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' shuffles only TIERS; the L for left stays in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Litres are metric units of volume, so they are measures.

clue.text: Fanciful upright type with idiosyncratic feature

parts.note: roman is upright printing type, as opposed to italic
a tic is a habitual quirk

explanation.surface: An imaginative, straight-laced person with a quirk.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic means idealised and imaginative, unrealistic.

clue.text: Place at table, lower head and scoff!

indicators.note: the first letter is moved further down, to the bottom of this down entry

parts.note: a seat is a place at a dinner table

explanation.surface: Sit down at dinner, bow your head, and tuck in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower head' moves the S of SEAT to the end. 'scoff' is British slang for eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is slang for wolfing food down, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: A very loud broadcast is happening!

parts.note: FF is fortissimo, the musical mark for very loud
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a noisy radio transmission is under way.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is an event or occurrence, a thing that takes place.

clue.text: Knocked out on leaving son in swamps

indicators.note: departing, so the word for on is removed

parts.note: floored means knocked down flat
RE means about or on, as in letter headings

explanation.surface: A boxer flattened after a son joins the fight in marshy ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes RE out of FLOORED to give FLOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: To flood is to swamp, deluge with water.

clue.text: Top Republican, drunk beyond question

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A senior Republican, plainly intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: An airtight case has no gaps, so it cannot be disputed.

clue.text: Calmly submissive, committed to further engagement

definitions.meaning: ..., put one's name to a contract again

explanation.definitionFit: Resigned means accepting one's fate; read as re-signed it means signed up once more.

clue.text: Bit of a kip invites efforts

parts.note: the kip is the currency of Laos, divided into 100 at
to tempt someone is to invite or entice them

explanation.surface: A short nap is tempting, it suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kip' looks like British slang for a nap, but here it is the Laotian currency unit, whose small coin is the at.
explanation.definitionFit: Attempts are tries, goes at doing something: efforts.

clue.text: Stage playwright succeeded, securing Oscar

indicators.note: holding something firmly inside, so the playwright word encloses the letter

parts.note: the Bard is Shakespeare, the playwright
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
S abbreviates succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A dramatist triumphs and wins an Academy Award for a production.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors 'tread the boards': the boards is the theatre stage itself.

clue.text: Scran cooked in ewers

indicators.note: prepared, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Food prepared in jugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Wieners are frankfurter sausages, an example of grub.

clue.text: Angry, ignoring short article's vision

indicators.note: leaving out, so the trimmed article's letters are removed from the word for angry

parts.note: seething means furious, angry

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: THE is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone cross, overlooking a brief item's point of view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims THE to TH, which 'ignoring' takes out of SEETHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing is sight, the faculty of eyesight.

clue.text: Fair maiden playing the violin topless?

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: with the top, the first letter, removed

parts.note: fiddling is informal for playing the violin

explanation.surface: A young woman bowing a violin with no top on, perhaps at a fairground.
explanation.definitionFit: Middling means of moderate quality, the same as fair in 'fair to middling'.

clue.text: Head of stinking fish for captain

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word

parts.note: a kipper is a smoked herring

explanation.surface: A smelly fish head served to the ship's captain.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is the master of a vessel or leader of a team.

clue.text: Degrading pre-eminent male following ill-doing

indicators.note: the male word comes after the wrongdoing word

parts.note: sin is wrongdoing
a king is the top man

explanation.surface: A top man falling from grace after misbehaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinking is going down, lowering in level or standard: deteriorating.

clue.text: Push five to quit Oxford?

indicators.note: the numeral leaves, so it is taken out of the word for push

parts.note: to shove is to push
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Pressing five people to leave Oxford University.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' looks like the city or university; the question mark marks it as an example, the Oxford lace-up.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford is a style of lace-up leather footwear, an example of the item.

clue.text: Guide quietly separating female and male on road

indicators.note: in a down clue, placed on top of the road
coming between, so the soft letter splits the two pronouns

parts.note: she is a female pronoun
he is a male pronoun
P is piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: A guide silently keeping a woman and man apart on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: To shepherd is to herd or steer people along, as a shepherd leads sheep.

clue.text: Salvation Army ways of handling 11, say

parts.note: usages are ways of using or treating

explanation.surface: The Salvation Army's methods of dealing with frankfurters.
explanation.definitionFit: Answer 11 is WIENERS, a kind of these, hence 'say' marking an example.

clue.text: By arrangement kept code concealed

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A secret code held back by agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Pocketed means put away out of sight, as in hiding something in a pocket.

clue.text: Repair part of 16, we're told

indicators.note: spoken out, so the word is given by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: 16 is SHOE, and the heel is part of a shoe

explanation.surface: A cobbler fixing a bit of a shoe, by report.
explanation.definitionFit: To heal is to mend or make whole again, as a wound.

clue.text: Dispute and squabble for Cock Robin's killer

parts.note: to spar is to argue
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Arguing about who did in Cock Robin.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme 'Who killed Cock Robin?', the answer is 'I, said the Sparrow, with my bow and arrow'.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme names this small bird as the one who shot Cock Robin.

clue.text: Marine creature's time to move rapidly without hesitation at first

indicators.note: lacking, so the first letter of the next word is removed

parts.note: to hurtle is to rush

indicators.note: the first letter of hesitation

explanation.surface: A sea creature hurrying along without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: A turtle is a shelled reptile living in the sea.

clue.text: Randomly despoiling when smashed lids removed for hoax

indicators.note: in no particular order, so the remaining letters are jumbled; 'smashed' and 'removed' tell us the scrambled lids are taken out

explanation.surface: Smashing tops off at random while looting.
explanation.walkthrough: Take L, I, D, S (lids, 'smashed') out of DESPOILING, then rearrange EPOING ('Randomly').
explanation.definitionFit: To pigeon is an old verb for swindle or dupe, like making a fool of someone.

clue.text: Advanced info over case of counterspy operation

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first pieces sit over the last

parts.note: gen is slang for information

indicators.note: the outer letters, the casing of the word

explanation.surface: Intelligence passed on about a double agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Agency means action or operation, as in 'by the agency of'.

clue.text: Grazing land beyond ancient city on banks of Euphrates

parts.note: past means beyond, as in 'past the church'
Ur was an ancient Sumerian city

indicators.note: the edges of the word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Fields for grazing outside an old city by the river Euphrates.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastures are grassy fields where livestock feed.

clue.text: Second piece about one going downhill

indicators.note: around, so the chess piece goes round the letter

parts.note: the king is a chess piece
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A further item on someone in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going downhill' suggests decline; here it is literal, a sport on snow slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing on snowy slopes literally takes you down a mountain.

clue.text: Ponder minute passage

definitions.meaning: to ... over is to study closely
a tiny opening in the skin

explanation.definitionFit: To pore is to study intently; a pore is also a tiny opening in skin.

clue.text: Description of Tudor monarch's interval of twelve semitones

definitions.meaning: Henry the ... was a Tudor king
an octave, which spans twelve semitones

explanation.definitionFit: Henry VIII's ordinal is this word, and in music the octave is also called the eighth.

clue.text: Roughly ten hours from London, for example

indicators.note: approximately, so the letters are taken loosely and rearranged

explanation.surface: A journey of about ten hours from the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: London lies in the south of England, so something from there is of that region.

clue.text: Keeping quiet, suffers meals prepared in particular way

indicators.note: holding within, so the word for suffers contains the hush

parts.note: dies, as in suffering death
SH is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone silently enduring food cooked a certain way.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishes are individual recipes or courses, food cooked in a certain style.

clue.text: Inclination to manage English clubs in US city

parts.note: to tend is to look after or manage

indicators.note: inside, so the card suit's letter sits within the city

parts.note: NY is New York
C abbreviates clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: A desire to run English nightclubs in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency is a leaning or disposition to act a certain way.
